summary.title: How to Write Your First Strategic Roadmap (Part 1)
summary.one_liner: A strategic roadmap is a guide built from goals, reasoning, route, ETA, risks, and explicit non-goals, not a feature list or work plan.
keywords: how to write a product roadmap
takeaways: A roadmap is a strategic guide and alignment tool, not a work plan or list of features and dates.
Start with at most one goal at a time for startups, framed in business terms, and prioritize goals before features.
Explain the reasoning behind goals and route in elaborated prose so readers can agree or disagree.
Build a plausible route of milestones, estimate ETA at roughly quarter granularity, and plan risks and mitigations in advance.
Explicitly state what you will not do, and exclude requests that do not fit the chosen route.
summary.summary: This first part of a three-part guide explains the components of a good strategic product roadmap: goal, reasoning, route, ETA, risks and mitigation, and what you are not going to do. The author argues that CEOs and product leaders should use the roadmap as a discussion tool to align on business goals before implementation. Each component is illustrated with examples, such as increasing POC-to-contract conversion or reducing churn. Parts 2 and 3, on the building process and on using the roadmap, were announced as forthcoming.
